Creativity for Kids Sensory Bin: Dinosaur Dig - Dinosaur Toys for Toddler Boys and Girls My child really likes this sensory bin. It’s a perfect indoor activity that has an outdoor activity feel (sand box and water table vibes). The sand is dense and forms well (kinetic play sand), and the water beads definitely give it a beach vibe. I added the small square bin inside to contain the water beads. I did not activate all of the water beads at once, that way we can make some fresh ones whenever we need to (they take about 3 hours to reach full size soaking in water).

One con is that the rim at the top of the bin itself is rough and very slim, and it leaves marks on our arms when we’ve played with it for a bit of time, which ends up being somewhat uncomfortable. A wider and more rounded rim on the bin would greatly improve the comfort while playing.

Another con is that the sand doesn’t sift very well with the yellow scooper. It’s perfect for shoveling the sand around, but not for sifting this denser type of play sand.

Despite some minor dislikes, the entire set is very entertaining for my preschooler, and it keeps us entertained as a fun winter activity.

text_fidelity_a:
Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig [[VIDEOID:f267642283bcf2ef6b127013dc46be9b]] On the advertising, this says that it shoots 20 feet. I was really skeptical, and I was expecting it to only shoot 20 feet in the air. Now, I don't have a 20 foot ladder, so I can't tell for sure, but I'm pretty sure that this will shoot vertically 20 feet, and horizontally maybe even a little more.

The truck is big and bulky, which I really liked. And there are no small, removable parts, so it's probably good for kids of any age. It does shoot a pretty powerful stream of water, so the only danger is squirting friends, family, and pets in the eye.

Now, about the water, the truck doesn't hold very much water. It says that it will shoot 50 shots of water, and it does do that. This is a lot like one of those water conserving showers. It really doesn't use very much water, but you can't really tell that until you fill it up. So, it's not the best thing for a water fight. But it is a great gift for youngsters so they don't get their siblings too wet. And I did really like the bright, vivid colors.

The wheels rotate, but they can't turn. If you need to turn this, you'll need to pick it up and move it around. Really, the only movable part on this is the fire hose.

Pros:
+Big and bulky
+Fun for all ages
+Shoots water a long way
+You can position the fire hose a little

Cons:
-A little hard to aim
-Wheels can't turn right or left, only rotate straight ahead
-Doesn't hold a ton of water
-You can't build up pressure to do a power squirt
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig

text_fidelity_a:
Baby Alive So Real Has a Boo Boo Blonde Baby Doll This Baby Alive Gets A Boo-Boo has a lot more playability than many of the other Baby Alive dolls- some of whom only talk or only do one or two things. The doll itself is all hard plastic, so she is not huggable. However, she has a removable dress, so she can wear other things, and it didn't take long for our girls to beg me to make this doll a nightgown and a white hospital gown to get her ready for a hospital bed so they can care for her.

The doll has a permanent band-aid on her knee, so when you open up the band-aid to look at her boo-boo, you will see the boo-boo change to all gone in a few looks. She also comes with a small array of band-aids and antiseptic, so the children can fix any boo-boos that this cute faced doll will get. Besides caring for her boo-boos, this Baby Alive comes with a bottle and a diaper, so you can feed and change her. You give her water and then have to change the wet diaper.

The only problem is with only one diaper, you will have to get her more diapers as the children find this feeding and changing fun. I took an old towel and cut up diapers for the girls. I added some velcro to be able to close the diaper without pins from the craft sewing store and now they have a supply of diapers that will dry over night- or if they can't wait- in the dryer for a few minutes. There is something about a doll that drinks, wets and gets boo-boos that makes the girls just love to take care of her. With an old towel, velcro and a hand made hospital gown, you will give your little caretakers hours of fun, making this doll well worth the money for a lot of fun play value.
text_fidelity_b: Baby Alive So Real Has a Boo Boo Blonde Baby Doll

LEGO NINJAGO Ninja Dragon Temple Set 71759 with Toy Motorcycle, Kai, NYA and Snake Warrior Minifigures, Gift for Kids 4 Plus Years Old LEGO have been hit by the inflation bug, and they've upped their prices recently on all sets. Nowhere is that more clear than in this set, which is very expensive for what you get.

Targeted towards the younger audience who is just beyond Duplo blocks, this is a pretty simple set with a pretty doofy-looking dragon that clearly skews younger, and doesn't fit in well with the rest of the Ninjago line, which is undoubtedly the LEGO line that has the highest "cool factor". So to judge this against a regular Ninjago set, this set woudl be a clear loser.

But it's really not for the older kids who can handle a ninja base or a 900-piece battle wagon, it's for littles. And for them, this is a fun set, but it is outrageously priced for what you get. It's essentially a few minifigs, a small dragon, a small set-piece, and a motorbike. Its simple to put together, but if you're working with a 4-year old, you probably need a little parental assistance.

For mini-munchkins, I suppose this would be a fun set to play with, but at close to $50 at the time of this writing, you are paying a very pretty penny for the fun you can have with it. At half that cost, and for the right audience, I'd find it a 4-star value. For what it is, I can't rank it higher than 3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO NINJAGO Ninja Dragon Temple Set 71759 with Toy Motorcycle, Kai, NYA and Snake Warrior Minifigures, Gift for Kids 4 Plus Years Old

Willking Pyramid Speed Cube 3x3x3 Pyraminx Speed Cube Triangle Puzzle Magic Cube This brought back many memories for me. I was a kid of the 80s, when the original Rubik's Cube came out. My parents were poor, so I could not get a genuine Rubik's Cube, but I got a knock off brand for Christmas that year. I have always been one of those brainy kids who likes mentally stimulating puzzles, games, and toys. My friends had these Pyraminx puzzles shortly after the Rubik's Cube came out and I have always wanted one. Now I have one.

This one is very nice. It turns easily and has bright, attractive colors. It is just the right size for my hands. I'm also quirky in that I like the box that it came in. It has illustrated instructions on how to solve, in Chinese, and a picture of a satisfied young man holding an acutal cube shaped cube on one side. He looks happy with himself so I guess this was fun for him. Or maybe he was saying, "I expected a pyramid one but a cube one came out of the box." Since I cannot read Chinese, I can only use my imagination about what this young man is saying about it. ETA I found out the man on the side of the box is the world record Rubik's Cube solving champion.

Back to the cube, this was a fun and nostalgic blast from the past. It was easy for me to solve. This is perfect for any child or adult who loves puzzles, challenges, or who fiddles a lot. It also makes an attractive and colorful desktop display. All in all, no complaints. It's great for any age.
text_fidelity_b: Willking Pyramid Speed Cube 3x3x3 Pyraminx Speed Cube Triangle Puzzle Magic Cube

LEGO NINJAGO Temple of Resurrection 70643 Building Kit (765 Piece) What I like with this LEGO set is that it does come with 7 mini figures. Makes it so much easier for me because I didn't have to run out to try to find some type of figures so the kids were able to play with this once they got it all built.
I let the older grandchildren go ahead and build this by themselves. It's getting hard for Paps to see all those smaller pieces anymore.
What was cute is that once they had it about 1/2 way built, they let the smaller kids pretend that the "warriors" were in command on getting their temple built. Because of that, they really helped keep the younger ones occupied for at least 3 days.
This is what I love about toys like this. Kids aren't glued to the tv, and kids aren't glued to their phones. They are using their brains and their hands to build something. Then they are using their brains to come up with a new adventure each time they play with it.
And, it's not set for just one age group. Yes, to build it the child has to be a certain age to understand the concept of putting it all together and reading the instructions. But, once it's all built the younger children (once they know not to put small items in their mouths or destroy what's built) can join in and play. Right now we have kids ranging from 4 1/2 to 12 playing with it. And when they grow older and lose interest in it, we pack up the entire set in zip baggies, add the instructions, and repack it into the box to save for the next generation of kids in the future.
I have always liked how well LEGOS are made. Parts are nice and sturdy and the colors on the blocks seem to last for years on end.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO NINJAGO Temple of Resurrection 70643 Building Kit (765 Piece)

LEGO Overwatch D.Va and Reinhardt 75973 Mech Building Kit with Popular Overwatch Character Minifigures and Buildable Rocket Hammer (455 Pieces) Neither my daughter nor I play Overwatch, but we do enjoy our Lego products together. I got this expecting to get some cool robots that would likely be invited over to tea with Barbie, but what I did not expect was how great these would look assembled. These robots have intricate touches on their armor that look really unique, and often hide the tell-tale Lego look that many of their creations have. The result is that these look more like real toys than something we put together.

There are a few minor quibbles. This comes with a lot of rare or unique pieces, but unlike a lot of kits, I have difficulty imagining using many of them beyond the specific applications of putting these kits together. A lot of very intricate and small pieces make these work. In addition, one of the figures slots into their robot perfectly, while the other is just tossed into a slot to rattle around, which feels pretty unfinished. A decidedly non-professional touch to a kit that would otherwise be worthy of display.

Overall though, a great character kit from Lego.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Overwatch D.Va and Reinhardt 75973 Mech Building Kit with Popular Overwatch Character Minifigures and Buildable Rocket Hammer (455 Pieces)

Klutz Crystal Unicorn Craft & Science Kit Crytal kits are notoriously iffy - sometimes they work, and sometimes they don't - and even the same kit will work sometimes, and not others. It has to be perfect, and I mean really perfect, for them to work at all.

For us, we ended up with crystals on only the base of the unicorn's tail and mane, and not on the tips (go figure). Those crystals are white or clear, and they look exactly like what they are - white crystals on a colored unicorn - not pink and blue crystals as the image on the box indicates.

Add to that the fact that there's roughly 1/3 of the items you'll need to make the kit included (you'll provide scissors, ruler, mason jars, distilled water, and a weight for the unicorn once you realize that it doesn't float), and this is a mediocre buy at best.

4DV5 Mini Drone for Kids with 720P Camera,FPV Live Video,LED Lights RC Quadcopter for Beginners,Boys and Girls Toys Gifts, Waypoints, Altitude Hold, Circle Fly,3D Flips,2 Battery,Orange First of all, my 9 year old son LOVED it! The LED lights are amazing and it was easy to watch in the dark at night, or just to enjoy during the day.

The "battery" is very different, you have to hook it up to the black device which has an USB and you need your own adapter to plug and recharge it. Each use lasts maybe 10 minutes max before you need to change batteries and recharge the first one. It is a great way to teach your child to take on different perspectives--if the drone is facing you, your left is actually its' right and your right is it's left. You have to consider that when using the controller just like with RC cars, except it is hard to tell from up in the air. You have to press left or right slightly to figure out which side then rotate it around so you can drive it. It comes with replacement spinners and a small screwdriver.

The return mode is nice, if you are freaking out and afraid it will go into a tree and unable to figure out which way to turn, just press that return button and it will come back to you.

Cons:
1. The drone was able to flip on the first day, but afterwards, for whatever reason, that stopped working. That didn't stop my son from enjoying it.
2. The video/camera app did not work on my phone. I tried different ways to get it to work.
3. Less than a week later, two of the "arms" that connect the ring to the base broke so now it won't lift up correctly. Even with superglue, that didn't help. Unfortunately, it is made of cheap flexible plastic.

So bottom line, I would not recommend buying this item.

This drone is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: 4DV5 Mini Drone for Kids with 720P Camera,FPV Live Video,LED Lights RC Quadcopter for Beginners,Boys and Girls Toys Gifts, Waypoints, Altitude Hold, Circle Fly,3D Flips,2 Battery,Orange

Lords of Waterdeep is a worker placement euro game through and through. You will be placing your "agents" out in waterdeep to recruit clerics, fighters, wizards and rogues to help you complete quests. Each Lord of Waterdeep has a specific objective for you to complete, like focusing on certain types of quests. You get points by completing quests and bonus points if those quests are of the type requested by your Lord.

This game has similar mechanics to Stone Age, Caylus and other worker placement games, but if you like Euro games and D&D, this is a great one to pick up. It plays in as little as an hour and even though the box says 12+ my 9 yr old plays it with ease.

Fisher-Price Imaginext Power Rangers Morphin Megazord This Imaginex Power Rangers Morphing Robot, is not a small toy. It hadn't registered when I'd ordered the figure, but it is over a foot wide and nearly 2.5 feet tall. While it's strong hard plastic, there are many moving parts, so it's best to transport it in its original box. It arrived via FedEx in a plastic sheath and the toy's original box. The moving parts are held down with plastic ties. I can see how unpacking/releasing the robot from the ties can be part of the fun for a kid. As I had planned to bring it to my nephew, I'm disappointed that it's too big to pack in carry on luggage.

The eyes light up when you move the robot's head. The hands can open and close their grip. The legs have secret compartments that open up to release rockets or that can serve as hiding places. There are 2 figurines that have perches - one on the shoulder and the other by the leg. The figure can move its torso but I haven't figured out how to make it walk yet.

I can imagine that it'll get my nephew excited and it's something that will interest his older sister as well.

FELVOR Oceanic Dolphin Animal Shaped Puzzle with Box Stand - 8 x 11 Inches Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - Challenging Wooden Animal Puzzle 150 Pieces There made in China and being sold by Chinese company colorful puzzles on Amazon right now. I don’t know how/why, but this one shows to be sold by a US company. Nonetheless, it is still made in China and it is still the same sort of puzzle that you will find a lot of on Amazon.

This one has very nice packaging. Some of these puzzles come in very plain cardboard boxes. But this one comes in a very nice wooden box with a laser cut out of the design on top. So you can use it, of course, for the puzzle pieces… But you can also use it for things like pencils… Candies… Stamps… And so on. So it is certainly a multipurpose sort of wooden box. And the design on top is great. The box also comes in a nice cardboard box, which makes this item very easy to give as a gift. Quick and easy wrapping. The wooden box measures just shy of 8” x 6” by one and three-quarter inches.

Though this puzzle has 150 pieces… Due to the fact that all of the pieces are very unique, and some of them are even of animals, this is not the easiest puzzle to put together. Which, I think is a nice thing. Some of the pieces are very small, so this is not the type of puzzle you will want to work around small children.

At the current price of twenty-five bucks this puzzle is a bit pricier than other options. If you look around, you will certainly find other puzzles for less… But… If what you really want is a dolphin puzzle, then this is a nice one.

Klutz Painted Rocks Craft Kit Multicolor, 10.5" Length x 0.75" Width x 8.5" Height This craft kit comes with a book on rock painting, eight acrylic paints, one paint brush, four pairs of self-adhesive googly eyes, and one rock. The kit is for ages 6 and up. The 40 page book comes with instructions on how to use the acrylic paints and included 28 step-by-step instructions for creating various paintings, from animals and flowers to various people, foods, and more. The book also contained pictures of other rock painting ideas but left it to the reader to figure out the steps needed to get the finished product. Most of these were pretty obvious and were similar to previous step-by-step projects.

The acrylic paints are white, black, blue, yellow, red, orange, green, and purple. Some of the designs required mixing these colors to make a new color, and adults may need to help younger kids with this. The paints had something in them to slow the drying time a little (so more like 30 minutes for dry to the touch rather than just a few minutes more typical for acrylic). This allowed for more time to make changes or mixing color on the rock.

The value in this kit is mainly the book as you only get one rock (thankfully...they're easy enough to get locally) and the painting supplies aren't going to go very far (maybe 10-20 rocks?). Still, this kit is enough to see if this is something your child enjoys. I painted the rock in the photo using the book instructions, but modifying the design to fit the rock.

text_fidelity_a: Puzzle Board with Drawers & Cover Mat - 1500 Pieces Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle Table - 40.5" X 27" Portable Puzzle Board with Cover for Adults & Children - Colorful Puzzle Trays for Sorting - Puzzle Ready This is a huge, sturdy puzzle board. It’s solid and well made and designed. The main area is large and easily holds my biggest 1000 piece puzzle. There are four drawers they pull out from the sides which are helpful in sorting pieces and keeping them safe when you aren’t working on the puzzle. They all have a different color of felt inside to help you keep track of what pieces are going where, which is useful for me since it tend to grab a handful and toss them in different piles. With the different backings it’s easier to know which pieces are where. The large rubber mat lays flat over the in progress puzzle so it stays in place when you put the board up. text_fidelity_a:
Arcade Claw Game: Maker Lab (Klutz STEM Kit) Brown/a, 9.8" x 2.5" x 11.8" The promise of this kit is that it's difficult. The final product, if it works according to specifications, looks amazing, and should teach some important concepts in a fun and interesting way. And this kit does accomplish a lot of what it sets out to do - it's hard to build, requires a little dexterity, and does work reasonably well after construction is complete - all while being a fun teaching tool.

This kit is labeled for use with smaller kids, but realistically a child will need to be around age nine or so to build this with minimal assistance from an adult. There are many steps, and it requires the ability to tie knots, balance pieces, and do some basic measurement.

Perhaps the strongest element of this kit is the booklet - steps are clear and easy to follow, although there are quite a few of them before a finished product is complete - and it does have a brief introduction that teaches the concepts of pulleys.

The downside of this kit is that, yes, it's difficult and time consuming. Unless your kid is an engineer in the making, it will require parental assistance. It's easy to quit, and if you do decide to leave it in the middle, it can be difficult to pick up where you left off. That said, difficulty is something that a lot of us want, so if you know it going in, then it's no big deal. The final product promises a lot, and surprisingly, it delivers, but the plastic side panels that hold the kit together are a bit flimsy, and require extra support.

Overall, we're impressed.
text_fidelity_b: Arcade Claw Game: Maker Lab (Klutz STEM Kit) Brown/a, 9.8" x 2.5" x 11.8"

Magic The Gathering: Arena of the Planeswalkers Game This is a great value for what you're paying. Essentially, this game is based on another very good game called Heroscape. You'll build an arena out of the little pieces in this box, create an army, and do battle with one of the prepainted Planeswalker minis.

I picked this game up as a former MtG player. I was hugely involved in the game from Ice Age through Darksteel. I invested thousands of dollars in the game until it finally became apparent that I couldn't afford to continue to be competitive in the game. What I love about this is that there is a little of what I like about MtG - the deckbuilding, the spellcasting and the strategy - but not so much of what I don't like - the cost.

The game itself is solid if not spectacular. It accomodates up to 5 relatively seamlessly, and it's easy to set up the game as a 2 vs. 2 if you like the team approach, or to just make it a free-for-all. The biggest problem to me with the game, enough to lower it two full stars, is that the game feels like it is missing some essential element that will be added through expansions. It's difficult to identify exactly what it is, but I can't shake the feeling that they took something essential out and going to release it as a big box expansion in the next few months.

As it is, it's a solid game that feels unfinished. I'll eagerly look forward to the (I"m assuming) forthcoming expansion.
text_fidelity_b: Magic The Gathering: Arena of the Planeswalkers Game

Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays I bought two packs of these bubble guns for a birthday party. You receive 2 pink guns and 3 blue guns in each pack. They are clear and have noise and lights.

Of the 10 bubble guns I received, 2 were defective. There is a lever that moves up and down to produce the bubbles. The lever is supposed to move when the trigger is pressed. For one of the defective bubble guns the lever was so tight that it rarely moved hence no bubbles. For the second defective bubble gun the rubber tubing was run the wrong way down the front of the gun so the rubber tube is very short. It produces bubbles but only when immersed in liquid in the bottle. It also spills a large amount of bubble liquid because of the defective tubing. After a short while it stops working because the bubble solution is too low in the bottle. My hand was also covered in solution at this point.

For the remainder of the bubble guns the rubber tubing is too long and they will not produce bubbles. The tubing is pressed against the side of the bubble container and is unable to siphon up the bubble liquid. The solution is to either push the tubing back up into the gun to make it about 1/4 inch shorter or to snip the end of the tubing by about 1/8 inch. The remaining 8 guns worked after I pushed the tubing higher.

I recommend you test the guns before handing them to children. I bought them for a birthday party so I tested them ahead of time to prevent disappointment.

These are different than battery operated bubble guns. For one thing, the lever has to be pressed about three times each time to produce bubbles in most of the bubble guns. For a few of the bubble guns a slow steady press produced a steady stream of bubbles but most of the triggers are too loose to allow a slow press. So the quality is inconsistent.

I paid $15.99 per box so from a value perspective I wasted about $6.36 because of the defective guns. I'll probably return one box.

UPDATE: Amazon shipped two replacement boxes but 5 of the 10 replacement guns were defective. I could not get them to work no matter how hard or long I tried. I shipped the defective bubble guns back. I will repeat my advice. Test each gun if you are using them for a party or event. Buy early enough so you have time to have replacements shipped to you. The ones that did work, worked beautifully. The kids enjoyed them.
text_fidelity_b: Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays

text_fidelity_a:
The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games First and foremost, this is a LIVING card game. It is not a COLLECTIBLE card game. Big difference! The latter just means that you can buy new expansions to expand your gameplay / add mechanics / etc. The latter means you have to go and buy packs at the store in order to get newer and better cards. In a collectible card game, a billionaire can go and buy all the packs and have the best deck ever. In this game, everyone who buys the game (and its expansion cards) will be on even footing. I find collectible card games to be somewhat predatory given they're essentially like gambling. Okay, on to the review.

High level message is, not great but not bad either. If you love Lord of the Rings you'll have a better experience. If you're neutral on it, then you're not going to enjoy the complicated grind of learning how to play.

Pros
- Beautiful artwork
- Good use of the LOTR lore in the gameplay and story
- Decent length of games - assume 1 to 1.5 hours
- Pretty good mechanics, once you understand them

Cons
- Phew, this game is complicated. The first sign that it's complicated, is the fact that there are TWO rule books, each of hefty size. This is not the kind of game you whip out on game night with a bunch of casual players. You need other folks who are dedicated to play this game, willing to watch a YouTube video together, or something, and then willing to stumble around for the first hour to get this done.
- So many things to keep track of... there's spinners, dials, tokens... did I mention this game is complicated
text_fidelity_b: The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

Educational Insights Kanoodle Jr. Brain Boosting Puzzle Game, Brain Teaser Game for Kids Teens, & Adults, 2-D & 3-D Puzzles, Great For Travel, Gift For Kids Ages 4 to 7 What a great puzzle. Kanoodle is a one-player game in which you take 6 tetris-like pieces and use them to fill in a pattern on the square board. There are 60 puzzles in this group, all included in a book form. I do have a few minor issues, enough to remove one star:

- The puzzles are delivered in the form of a book. There are multiple languages of instructions inside, then you get to the puzzles. Each puzzle is well-done, but the book itself is not the ideal way of presenting the puzzles. Since you're either balancing the book on the shelf above the board, or pulling it out or putting it back underneath the board, it gets scuffed, torn and bent up rather quickly. On day 3, our book looks like a mess. It should have been thicker cards with a separate rulebook.

- Some kids will master this quickly. My four-year-old is on 4-star puzzles already, and we've owned the game for less than 3 days. I think she'll be stuck here for a decent while, and she does enjoy going back to re-do easier puzzles, but I think she's got the hang of it quickly. Yesterday, she completed puzzle 43 out of 60, and they're ordered by difficulty.

This review may sound negative, but let me emphasize that THIS IS SUCH A GOOD TOY! You can see the wheels turning in my daughter's brain as she tries to figure out how to make it work. If you're going on a road trip, this is a must.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Kanoodle Jr. Brain Boosting Puzzle Game, Brain Teaser Game for Kids Teens, & Adults, 2-D & 3-D Puzzles, Great For Travel, Gift For Kids Ages 4 to 7

KLUTZ Make Your Own Mini Erasers Toy includes (8)colors of eraser clay^pencil^clay shaping tool^(2)sheets of papercraft displays I had some low expectations after reading some of the reviews that people posted about this craft kit. Still the price was reasonable so I ordered one. This is not the first Klutz craft kit we've played with - so it was a familiar experience as those other kits. There really wasn't much in the box - the clay, a pencil (without an eraser), a sculpting tool, and a couple sheets of foldable paper props for the erasers you make (if you make the ones shown in the instructional guide).

You get plenty of different color clay - if you limit yourself to making fairly small erasers. The clay we got wasn't dried out - but it did take some kneeding to get soft enough to shape. Baking the erasers was simple - we used a toaster oven. Just be sure to use the right temperature and watch the erasers while they bake to make sure none start melting. Baking time can vary - mostly 15 to 30 minutes depending on the size & shape of the erasers you made.

The erasers are more ornamental than practical - but they do erase most pencil marks.

We're having fun with this kit - the instructional guide is outstanding. I'm happy with my purchase.

Learning Resources Botley The Coding Robot - 45 Pieces, Ages 5+ Screen- Free Coding Toys, Coding STEM Toy for Kids, Coding for Kids,Back to School Gifts,Teacher Supplies Botley is quite a versatile fellow.

My four year old is having fun running him around in "line" mode, where his sensors follow a black lined path on a white background. When he reaches the end, he turns around and comes back.

Daddy is having a little more fun with "code" mode, which is too complex for the little one at this point. You program multiple commands into the remote, and then you send Botley out on a small adventure, around the obstacle course pieces that you can set up with material from the box. It's simple and easy for an adult, but for kids, it will teach computer programming basics, planning ahead, and thinking before you act.

The box comes with a variety of cones, bricks and blocks, as well as arms for Botley and cards that can help you measure how far he's going to move, and doubles as a wavy black line pattern on the reverse side if you want to use it. All told, it's a fun and complete package, although I wish the instructions were a little more explicit for adults, and a little more fun for little ones to explore on their own. As it stands, the manual explains a few little tasks you can try, written in tiny font in as few pages as humanly possible. I want more from this.

Stay away.

text_fidelity_a:
Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA The loom is intended to make it easier to make braid or bead bracelets. The 6 spools come pre-wrapped with different types of cording. I didn't particularly care for their pre-wrapped selection, however, the spools can be wrapped with whatever cord or thread you want to use. Then you pop the spools into the dispenser section of the loom and slide the axle into place. We had some trouble getting the axle out again. The spools stay in place just fine without the axle, so we have no plans to use it again. You measure out 8 to 12 inches of cord for each strand to create a braided bracelet. You slip the cord into the foam slots near the spools to hold the cord in place, then braid using your own design or the instruction booklet directions. The booklet describes how to make a 3 strand braid, 6 strand braid, braided bracelet where one strand is first beaded, and a friendship bracelet. Though well-illustrated, the instructions were not always clear.

For beaded bracelets, you remove the green foam insets, choose a beading pattern, and set up the beads on the tray. The tray does make threading the beads easier. You place cords on either side of the beads on the board and use the included needle and thread to string the beads and attach them to the cords in rows. Except for the axle, everything worked fine. It would have been nice if the beads were packaged in sealed in zip bags or the like as they keep spilling. I ended up finding bags to put them in.
text_fidelity_b: Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA

text_fidelity_a:
Pressman Original Retro Style Large Numbers Rummikub - Includes Tiles with Bright, Over-Sized, Inset Numbers for Easy Viewing, Multi Color This game is such a classic! I literally played the original version of Rummikub everyday in the summer at my grandma’s house growing up in the 80s & 90s. The concept of the game is simple and easy to learn (making sequences, and the joker faces can be anything you need like a wild card). I’m not sure what happened to our family’s original old set, so I’m thrilled to have a new version for our game closet.

The actual tiles have a slightly different look but do feel the same as the old ones I remember. I do miss the small circles at the bottom of each tile from the old version—they seemed easier to grab onto with that little finger spot. One thing worth mentioning is that this set doesn’t have a storage pouch for the tiles, which I think certain versions do include—this one does not, and I don’t mind at all.

This is an excellent game for kids and family game night. It’s something to get your mind thinking, strategizing, but it’s also simple and fun. I loved playing it this evening with one of my siblings, as it was like the good old days! Highly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Pressman Original Retro Style Large Numbers Rummikub - Includes Tiles with Bright, Over-Sized, Inset Numbers for Easy Viewing, Multi Color

Olefun Sight Words Flash Cards with Characters Scene & Motion & Sentences-220 Educational Flash cards for Age of 4,5,6,7 Years old,Pre K,Preschool, Kindergarten,1st,2nd Grade,Homeschool,Learn to Read. These Sight Words cards are great overall. I especially like that multiple levels come in one box, so it can work great for multiple ages in one home, or grow with a single child for several years. We are at level 1, so we will get a lot of use from this set.

Using the cards, I show my child an image with a word on the front side, and then I have notes on the backside for each word. I improvise a lot with these cards by asking my child to do different things that I think make more sense for the room we’re playing in, but sometimes I also use the suggestions on the back. We think it’s fun, and it’s a great learning opportunity to become familiar with how sight words look, while playing by acting out what the words mean.

One observation that struck me as odd is the text for the letter K. I do not believe children are taught to read or write this letter in this format, so I feel it is an odd choice. Otherwise, this kit is a great learning tool for kids!
